- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid missing reversal.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged decline; add a “lag correction” — delay peak forecast by 1–2 days and reduce magnitude.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch momentum; increase forecast slope or add a “sentiment momentum” multiplier (e.g., +0.5x for 3–5 days).
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–14 day windows; if forecast is > 2σ above recent mean, reduce by 1–3% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment confirms breakout.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates late-period spikes (especially after sentiment turns bullish); apply “late-period bias” — add 0.5–1.5% to final 5–7 days if sentiment > 0.67 in last 3 days.
